hard_case: RIPR-SPEC-0263 example 1. Measured defect (#7132): the direct-collection observer credits `assert_eq!(v, Vec::<u32>::new())` as revealing the push, so call_deletion and side_effect read exposed, although the only related test calls add(&mut v, 4) and 4 never enters `x > 10`. No mutant of the push executes under the test.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: add(&mut v, 11) records nothing

reasoning: adds_nothing_for_small_values calls add(&mut v, 4); 4 > 10 is false, so the push never runs and every mutant of it passes. The empty-vector equality would notice a wrong push only if some test input entered the guard.
